newsitem.title: GERMANY: German trade with HK to continue growing -business.
newsitem.headline: German trade with HK to continue growing -business.

text.p: Hong Kong will remain the pivot for German trade with China and the rest of Asia, German business leaders said on Monday, the last day of British rule.
Michael Fuchs, president of the German Association of Wholesale and Foreign Trade (BGA), said China's resumption of sovereignty over the British colony would not harm trade.
Since Hong Kong will remain autonomous in everything but defence and foreign policy, trade will continue to grow, he said.
"China will want to maintain face and show the world that Hong Kong's previous success was not dependent on Britain," Fuchs said.

"China has a vital interest in the continued economic development of the Hong Kong special administrative zone," he said. "For most business-oriented Hong Kong Chinese, the handover means 'business as usual'."
Germany is Hong Kong's fourth largest trading partner after China, the United States and Japan.
Its exports to Hong Kong rose to 6.4 billion marks ($3.7 billion) in 1996 from 3.5 billion in 1991, and will grow 12 to 14 percent this year to 7.7 to nine billion marks, Fuchs forecast.
German imports from Hong Kong fell 5.4 percent in 1996 to 3.5 billion marks.
Franz Schoser, a leading executive of the German Federation of Chambers of Commerce (DIHT), said, "Many reservations that people had in the beginning have evaporated.
"There will still be a little bit of nervousness but I believe China will not try to implant a new system in Hong Kong. We can be confident things will continue," Schoser said in a radio interview.
One-third of Germany's trade with China is routed through Hong Kong, Schoser said.
Wolfgang Ehrmann, DIHT's representative in Hong Kong, said the economic reunification of Hong Kong with the mainland took place long ago. Now political reunification is following.
"As long as state influence remains small, there is no danger of an increase in corruption," he told German television.
-- Terence Gallagher, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-2609750 ($ = 1.739 German Marks)
